rules.name: Data Science Core
rules.notes:
Pre-Approved Substitutions: We recommend all students take the standard courses shown above. However, to provide flexibility, students may use up to two of the following pre-approved substitutions within the Data Science Core without additional approval. Students requesting more than two substitutions must submit the Data Science Requirement Inquiry Form and obtain approval from the program directors.

• Required course: MATH 104 | Approved substitution: ENGR 108

• Required course: STATS 117 | Approved substitutions: CS 109, MS&E 120, or EE 178

• Required course: STATS 191 | Approved substitutions: MS&E 125 or MS&E 226
Advanced Alternatives: Students interested in more advanced alternatives to the standard courses may also choose from the following. Students may take any number of advanced alternatives:

• Required course: MATH 51 | Advanced alternatives: MATH 61CM or MATH 61DM

• Required course: MATH 104 | Advanced alternative: MATH 113

• Required course: STATS 117 | Advanced alternative: STATS 118

• Required course: STATS 191 | Advanced alternative: STATS 200 or STATS 200Q or STATS 203

• Required course: MS&E 111, MS&E 111DS, or MS&E 111X | Advanced alternative: EE 364A

rules.name: Pathway
rules.desc: The pathway is an opportunity for students to develop specific expertise on a topic they are passionate about and where data science methods and approaches have something compelling to offer. Students must choose one of the following pathways or develop their own, with guidance and approval from the program.

children.name: Brains & Behavior
children.desc:
Complete seven total courses, at least two from each category (Foundation, Intersection, Context).
Courses must span at least two social science disciplines (communication, economics, political science, psychology, and sociology).

rules.name: WIM for Students in Social Systems Subplan
rules.desc:
Most students pursuing the Data Science B.A. with the social systems subplan will complete the Data Science Practicum (DATASCI 192A/B), which double-counts to satisfy both the capstone and WIM requirements.
In special instances, students can apply to fulfill the capstone requirement through conducting an independent data science research project under the supervision of a professor (see capstone requirement for more details), in which case they must take DATASCI 120 to satisfy the WIM requirement.

children.name: Data Narratives (with an independent research capstone)

rules.name: Capstone for Students in Social Systems Subplan

children.name: Data Science Practicum
children.desc: Most students pursuing the Data Science & Social Systems B.A. will complete the Data Science Practicum (DATASCI 192A/B) for their capstone, which double-counts to satisfy both the capstone and WIM requirements.

children.name: Independent Research Project
children.desc:
In special instances, completing DATASCI 120 and an independent research project in data science could also be considered for the capstone requirement; the project must be pre-approved by the program directors, substantially use techniques from upper-division Data Science coursework, connect to a social issue (typically related to the student’s pathway), and be completed during senior year.

• By the final study list deadline of autumn quarter during senior year, students should join the Canvas page for Independent Research Projects.

• During autumn quarter of senior year, students should find a professor who agrees to supervise the research project.

• By the last day of classes of autumn quarter, students must complete the Proposal to Use Independent Research for Data Science & Social Systems B.A. Capstone form, have it approved by the research advisor, and submit it to the Canvas page for Independent Research Projects. Approval must be obtained from the program directors through this process.

• Students should enroll in DATASCI 199 (independent study) for a letter grade with the supervising professor in every quarter until they finish conducting the research and creating the report/poster.

• To complete the capstone, the student must submit a final report and approval form signed by their research advisor.
Students who use an independent research project to fulfill the capstone requirement will need to take DATASCI 120 (Data Narratives) to fulfill the WIM requirement. DATASCI 120 complements independent research, and it can be taken before or concurrently with working on the project.

grading: All courses that fulfill major requirements must be taken for a letter grade. Students may be granted a one-time exception to use one course taken for credit (CR) toward the major. This exception does not apply to the WIM and capstone, which must always be taken for a letter grade.
policies:
All students must choose a subplan.
Double-counting within the major is not allowed, unless explicitly stated otherwise. The major follows the university policy on double-counting between the data science major and another major or minor, including the list of approved courses here.
transferPolicy: The program must approve transfer credit before it can be applied toward Data Science major requirements. First, students should submit the course-to-course equivalency request form. After receiving a decision on that request (whether approved or denied), students should submit the request to apply transfer credit toward the Data Science major. Requests are reviewed on a case-by-case basis by the Program Director and Associate Director. Please see our Transfer Credit page for more information.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the Data Science Core (up to two of the listed pre-approved substitutions, and any number of the advanced alternatives), then your subplan's own Extended Core, WIM and capstone, with every course letter graded and counted toward one requirement only. The exceptions the text makes are the Data Science Practicum (DATASCI 192A and 192B), which counts as both your WIM and your capstone in Social Systems, and DATASCI 120, which is the WIM inside the independent research capstone. In the Social Systems subplan each pathway takes seven courses, two from each category plus one more; in the Artistic and Cultural Analysis subplan your primary pathway takes two foundation classes, one foundation class from each of two other pathways (15 units in all) and 12 advanced units, and any HISTORY 200 Doing History seminar counts as an Archive foundation class. You check by hand the one CR course the program may allow, a third core substitution or a CS 106A waiver, pathway and capstone approvals, the unit minimums some pathway courses carry (DATASCI 199 at 2 units, EARTHSYS 106 at 5, ENERGY 177A/B at 3 each), the self-designed pathway and the Capstone Showcase.
